rationale: The edit adds an else-if branch for the mailtrap transport to an env-driven transport chain that now has five branches (sendmail, ses, smtp, mailgun, mailtrap plus a fallback). Each branch builds its own collaborators (require of a vendor SDK, option objects, a token check that throws) and creates its own transporter, so this is not a one-line-per-variant registry: adding the next transport means editing this chain again. Shape 2, chain >= 3 branches after the edit, so the branch addition is worsened and currentConcern holds in the after code.

The edit refactors sumDraftCounts into link collection plus batched DB counting; it adds no case or else-if branch and the attribute-type switch keeps the same three branches (relation, component, dynamiczone) as before. That switch is a recursive reducer over the closed set of schema attribute types that traverses the model, which the closed-grammar/visitor exception covers, so the after state holds no violating chain; the edit itself is unchanged.

The edit splits the shared case string/text into two separate cases so string can carry maxLength.max(255); it adds a case label but no new attribute-type variant, and each branch only returns a declarative yup validator-shape object (a table of validation config per type in disguise) rather than variant behaviour with own statements or collaborators. The dispatch is over the closed set of schema attribute types, so no violation is introduced and the after state holds no violating chain; unchanged.

The edit adds two observation cases (submission_queued, submission_settled) to the switch over @flue/runtime observation types. That switch is a reducer over an event grammer owned and closed by an external library, and every pre-existing branch already delegates to a per-event helper (startTurnSpan, endTurnSpan, startToolSpan, endToolSpan), which the closed-grammar/visitor exception covers; the two new cases only record and drop an admission entry. No new extension point is created, so no nudge and no concern in the after state.

The edit only rewrites Next.js pathname patterns to TanStack route patterns (/sql/[id] to /sql/$id) and swaps push for navigate; it adds no branch, no case, and no new comparison, so the edit itself is unchanged and must not notify. The scope does still hold the same else-if ladder over routePattern that calls a different last-visited setter per route — dispatch on a route name tag with per-variant behaviour, and the route set keeps growing — so currentConcern stays true as tracked debt.

The edit adds three cases (string-array, milliseconds, bytes) to the type-to-converter switch in cast(), but each branch only maps a tag to one converter handler (toString, toNumber, toBytes, toMilliseconds) or a two-step array map; this is the designated value-conversion registry where a variant costs one line, and the surrounding edit is also moving converters into their own utils (to-boolean.js, to-bytes.js, get-type-map-entry.js). No variant behaviour with own collaborators or I/O moves in, so no nudge and no concern.

The edit extracts the error-type to status-code switch out of the express handler into an exported getHttpResponseFromError without adding, removing or reordering a branch; each branch only assigns a status code and constant body fields, a data mapping over MedusaError.Types, a closed library enum. That is a table in disguise / closed stable set, so the edit is unchanged and the after state holds no violating chain.

The only change is reordering the existing cases inside the field-type switch (collapsible/row first, then group, number/text/textarea, tabs); no case, else-if or condition is added, so this edit is unchanged and must not notify. The switch itself walks the field schema, a recursive reducer over the schema attribute grammar, which the closed-grammar exception covers, so no concern remains.

The edit adds case openrouter to the config.type switch in createAIProviderRegistry, which is the designated composition point for providers: every branch maps a tag to one constructor call (createOpenAI, createGoogleGenerativeAI, createOpenRouter, createOpenAICompatible) and feeds createProviderRegistry, one variant per case. That is the factory/registry exception, so the added branch is not a violation and there is no concern.

The edit adds a fallthrough case 23001 to an existing SQLSTATE-code case that already returns ForeignKeyConstraintViolationException. The switch maps a closed, stable set of PostgreSQL error codes to exception classes, each branch a single constructor call, i.e. the designated tag-to-handler mapping point, so the added case is not a violation and the after state holds none.

load() replaced a KNOWN_MODULES array plus one dynamic require with a switch on the module name, one literal require per case, because bundlers must statically trace those requires (stated in the added comment); the previous shape was a table, so no new extension debt is created. Each branch is a single-line tag-to-handler entry in the one place where driver modules are composed, which is the registry exception, hence no nudge and no concern.

The edit extends the geometry case to also cover the concrete geometry.<Shape> type names (geometry.Point, geometry.LineString, ...), all falling through to one existing branch. Every branch of the switch only returns a constant list of operator strings, which is the pure-value-mapping exception (a table in disguise), so nothing new is hidden behind the chain and the edit is unchanged.

The edit replaces two ifs and a boolean return with a switch over Sec-CH-Prefers-Contrast values and returns a result object naming its source. Each branch only returns a constant object (custom/less/no-preference to false, forced/more to true, default to the fallback), a pure value mapping, and the header value set is closed by the client-hint spec; so the new three-branch chain does not violate the rule and the edit does not notify.

The edit reorders the HTTP-status cases in handleError, throws instead of returning in the default branch, and gates the new environment-creation step on config.featureFlags.asyncProjectCreationEnabled. A switch over HTTP status classes is a closed, stable set, and the new branch is a feature flag, both explicit exceptions, and no per-variant branch behaviour is added to a type-dispatch chain, so the edit is unchanged and holds no concern.

The edit replaces regex matching with parseRoutePattern plus a new recursive scoreMatch whose switch dispatches on RouteSegment.kind (static, param, optional, splat). That union is a closed four-variant grammar declared in this same module and the switch is an exhaustive matcher/parser over it, which the closed-grammar visitor exception covers, so the new function does not create an open extension point and there is no concern. Uncertainty: a stricter reading could treat the four per-kind recursive branches as introduced.

The edit adds case enterpriseNotice to Block, a switch on block.kind that already holds a branch per doc-block variant (markdown, heading, typeList, workflowDiagram, codeTabs, note, linkList, badges, ...). Several branches carry their own collaborators and mapping logic (codeTabs builds one CodeTab per tab, linkList builds Ul/Li/Anchor, badges maps variants), so this is not a one-line tag-to-handler table: adding the next block kind means editing this growing conditional again. The branch is added to an existing 3+ chain, so impact is worsened and currentConcern holds.

The edit introduces a switch on operationType ("save" | "remove" | "soft-remove" | "recover") in place of one compound boolean, and each branch only assigns a boolean from relation cascade flags; the union is closed and declared in the method signature. That is a pure value mapping over a closed, stable set, so no variant behaviour is held inline, the edit is unchanged and no concern remains.

The edit keeps the existing else-if chain on relation.inverseRelation.orphanedRowAction (nullify, delete, soft-delete), which is a closed three-value set owned by the relation metadata, and adds a nested if on whether the join columns are nullable inside the nullify branch. That nested condition is a guard on column nullability, not a new variant tag, and every branch only assigns subject flags, so nothing new is hidden behind the chain; the edit is unchanged and holds no concern.

The new cleanMorphToManyOrderColumn carries a switch on db.dialect.client with one case (mysql) and a default, so the chain has only two branches after the edit; the rubric says fewer than three branches is too early to call. The edit is a new function that adds no branch to an existing chain, so no nudge and no concern (uncertainty only on whether the dialect split should later grow a table).

The edit adds a second if on event.data.type (STRAPI_FIELD_SINGLE_CLICK_HINT) beside the existing focus-intent if, and a two-branch instanceof check (PreviewFieldError then Error) in the catch. Both chains have two branches after the edit, which is too early to call, and they dispatch on message events and error classes rather than a growing variant tag; the edits only swap inline strings for PREVIEW_ERROR_MESSAGES entries, so unchanged with no concern.

The restructured load() turns one ternary into an if/else on whether projectId is defined and grows the catch into if (isPreviewNotConfigured(error)) / else if (state === ready) / else. Those conditions are error and state guards, not dispatch on a variant tag holding per-variant behaviour, and the remaining state assignment is a nested ternary that only assigns constant state names (pure value mapping). No chain becomes a violation, so no nudge and no concern.

The only change is comparing asset.type against ASSET_TYPES members instead of AssetType members; the shape of the chain is untouched and it only assigns a translated label per asset type, a pure value mapping over a closed asset-type set. No nudge, no concern.

The edit swaps snap.onEditTable and friends for handlers from useTableActions; no case is added to the EntityActionId switch (copy-name, copy-schema, copy-definition, edit-table, duplicate-table, export-csv, export-sql, export-cli, view-partitions, delete), and each case is a single handler call in the one place where entity actions are wired, which the registry/composition-point exception covers. The nested if on entity.type in delete is unchanged, so the edit is unchanged and no concern remains.

The edit adds case sveltekit.endpoint to _getKitSpanOrigin, a switch that maps a SvelteKit span name to a constant origin label; every branch only returns a constant (the handle.root case returns undefined on purpose), which is the pure value mapping exception over a closed set of library span names. No nudge and no concern.

The edit extracts getPropertyKeyName, renamePropertyKey and migrateSslValidate out of the forEach body and reorders nothing that matters; the same four property-name checks remain, and those are table-driven lookups (removeProps set, simpleRenames record, writeConcernProps set) over a fixed list of deprecated Mongo options rather than a chain that holds each variant behaviour inline. The edit adds no branch, so unchanged and no concern.

The edit adds a branch on schema shape in _getQueryParameters (expandable object properties, deepObject style, plain) and a recursive _resolveSchema with branches on object/allOf/anyOf/oneOf. Those conditions are shape predicates, not equality on a variant tag, and _resolveSchema is a transformer over the closed JSON Schema composition grammar, the closed-grammar exception, so no dispatch chain a new variant must edit is created and the edit is unchanged.

The new file upload-to-provider.ts creates a switch on the provider kind with four branches, each checking its own API key and calling its own adapter (uploadToOpenAI, uploadToAnthropic, uploadToGoogle); a new provider has to edit this chain, so the after code does hold a growing type-dispatch chain with inline variant behaviour. notify is still false because the file did not exist before (before null), so this is a creation, not an extension the rule reviews.

The file is new (before null), so this is a creation, not an extension the rule reviews, and notify is false. Its one chain, the switch on field.type in the recursive comparison, has only the array/blocks and group branches plus default over the closed set of schema field types — a schema visitor, not a growing dispatch — so the after code holds no violating chain either.

The file is new (before null), so notify is false on the creation rule. The provider switch has only two cases (langfuse, braintrust) plus a default that warns and returns, which is fewer than three branches and too early to call, and the required-key lookup is already a table, so no concern is present in the after code.

The file is new (before null), so it is a creation and notify is false. buildTransport is the single factory that maps config.type to a transport construction, one createTransport call per variant with that variant option shape, which the factory exception covers, so the after code holds no violating chain.

The file is new (before null), so this is a creation and notify is false. documentReducer is a switch on action.type over a closed discriminated-union action set, which the reducer-over-a-closed-grammar exception covers explicitly, so no violating chain remains in the after code.

The file is new (before null), so notify is false on the creation rule. statusColor only maps a closed AdminSearchIndexStatus union to constant colour names, a pure value mapping in table form, so no violating chain is present.

The file is new (before null), so notify is false on the creation rule. Its coerce switch maps PlannedField.kind (number, boolean, text/keyword, vector) to a conversion call and returns the value unchanged in default, which is a pure value mapping over a closed kind union, so no violating chain is present.

The file is new (before null), so notify is false on the creation rule. groupAttachments is a switch on the closed ContextAttachment type union that only groups attachments into buckets, and the per-variant formatting already lives in separate formatter functions; that grouping reducer is the closed-union exception, so no violating chain is present in the after code.

The edit adds an else-if that suppresses the warning for two known paths (a Set membership guard on the request pathname) beside the existing validity check. It is a path guard, not a branch on a variant tag holding variant behaviour, and the chain has two branches, so no nudge and no concern.

The edit adds a state guard in the catch: reject only when the transaction has not started, and rethrow errors that are not the rollback signal. That is a guard on two boolean/identity conditions, not dispatch on a variant tag, and the edit adds no branch to an existing chain, so it is unchanged with no concern.

The edit adds JsonText plus wrapGridJsonText, and inside the SQL value serialisation adds an instanceof JsonText branch and an empty-ARRAY guard. That chain formats one scalar expression per JS value kind (null, ARRAY, JsonText, json, text, number, boolean, other) and holds no variant behaviour with own state or collaborators, so it is a value-mapping chain, not the growing type-dispatch chain shape 2 refers to; unchanged, no concern (uncertainty: shape 2 names instanceof branches).

The edit adds piAiSystemInstructions, piAiToolDefinitions, piAiSystemMessages and piAiContentText, built from loops and plain guards (typeof, isObjectLike, Array.isArray); the piAiPartToGenAiPart switch on part.type is untouched and only maps each part kind to a constant object. No dispatch chain grows, so the edit is unchanged and holds no concern.

visibleTo becomes a filter composer: it pushes one where clause per scope the caller asked for (instance, user, project) instead of picking one branch, so the conditions accumulate rather than dispatch, and the unchanged whereTarget switch maps each scope tag to a constant where object (pure value mapping). No chain grows, so unchanged with no concern.

The edit turns the final else in nextRouterInstrumentNavigation into else if (process.env._sentryHasPagesRouter !== 0 false) so bundlers can drop the Pages Router navigation module. That is a build-time flag guard on a two-branch conditional, a feature-flag branch rather than dispatch on a variant tag, so no nudge and no concern.

The edit threads a new oppositeCollection field through getRelationInfo and derives it with a two-branch if/else-if on relationType (o2m, a2o or m2o); two branches is too early to call and the conditions select a field, not a variant handler. No chain grows, so unchanged with no concern.

The edit adds a fast oxc transform path (lazily imported) before falling back to transformWithBabel, which is the same body moved into a helper; the remaining branches are two-way guards on file name endings and the injectIntoHtml flag. No tag-dispatch chain grows, so unchanged with no concern.

Unchanged, no concern.

The edit adds a custom-order block to updateContentTypeConfiguration: a feature-flag check (isCustomOrderFeatureEnabled) plus guards on whether input.settings carries customOrder and whether the type is orderable, returning a 400 when not. Those are feature-flag and validation guards, not branches on a variant tag, so no nudge and no concern.
